samples.summary: notes-view now remounts on `readOnly`, but `YorkieNoteStore` has no `dispose()` — its constructor `doc.subscribe(...)` is never released, so every editor→viewer downgrade leaks a subscribed store bound to a disposed editor
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143` subscribes in the constructor and discards the returned unsubscribe; the class has no `dispose()`. `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:150-155` cleanup only does `editor.dispose(); storeRef.current = null` — it never releases the store, yet `notes-view.tsx:167` now lists `readOnly` in the effect deps, creating a remount path that did not exist before. This is precisely the hazard the diff fixed for docs (`docs-view.tsx:574` `store.dispose()` + new `YorkieDocStore.dispose()`) and that slides already handles (`slides-view.tsx:1216`). Impact here is bounded (the leaked subscription only calls `captureHistorySelection()`, which writes a private field), so it is a leak plus a stale listener rather than a stray CRDT write.

samples.summary: Three sibling stores and two design docs still point at `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`, a field this change renamed to `undoFloorMark`/`undoFloorDepth`
samples.evidence: Stale references to the removed name: `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:125` ("Mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`"), `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:345` (same phrase), `packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:49` ("because it reads its `undoFloor`" — the diff updated the identical comment inside `yorkie-doc-store.ts` but not this one), `docs/design/notes/notes.md:399`, `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:183-209` and `:323` ("Reference impls: `docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` (Docs, with `undoFloor`)"). Each now describes a contract the reference implementation no longer has. Nested design docs are not covered by the docs link check, so nothing else catches these.

samples.summary: The length-vs-depth undo floor this change replaced for docs (#1045) still exists verbatim in the slides, notes and board stores, which are all capped by the same 50-entry Yorkie stack
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:654` (`getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`), `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:353`, and `packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:514` all keep the absolute-depth comparison whose failure mode the diff documents at length (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:590-600`: once `pushUndo` `shift()`s entries off the bottom, the recorded depth stops describing the boundary and `canUndo()` refuses reachable undos). Not broken *by* this change — but the diff establishes the correct pattern in one of four identical implementations, so the other three are now knowingly out of step, and slides/notes/board reach the cap the same way (per-element writes, `MaxUndoRedoStackDepth = 50`).

samples.summary: `YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH = 50` hard-copies the SDK's unexported `MaxUndoRedoStackDepth`; an SDK bump silently changes which branch of `canUndo()` runs
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:571` duplicates a constant the SDK does not export, and `canUndo()` (`:3062`) uses `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` to distinguish "floor shifted off the bottom" from "entry rebuilt in place" — i.e. to decide whether to latch the floor open. SDK bumps are a live activity in this repo (`docs/tasks/active/20260909-yorkie-0720-bump-todo.md`), and node_modules is not installed here so I could not confirm the current value. The diff argues drift is safe in one direction only; a *smaller* real cap leaves the depth fallback (over-restrictive), a larger one is absorbed — but nothing in CI ties the two together, so the reasoning has to be re-derived by hand at every bump.

samples.summary: `writePageSetup` still writes the raw `docStore`, so a second page-setup write path exists outside the new revocable handle — contradicting the comment the diff adds at editor.ts:3310
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2299-2311` (`writePageSetup`) calls `docStore.setPageSetup(...)` on the *raw* store. The diff deliberately routed the parallel `guardedSetPageSetup` through `revocableStore` and calls it "the single page-setup-shaped hole left in a disposed handle" (`editor.ts:3310-3313`), but this one was left on the raw store. It is currently unreachable after disposal — `api.setPageSetup` is `writePageSetup` (`editor.ts:3473`) and is in `MUTATING_METHODS`, and the other driver, `ruler.onMarginChange` (`editor.ts:2314`), loses its `document` mouseup listener in `Ruler.dispose()` (`packages/docs/src/view/ruler/index.ts:460-468`, bound at `:385`). So no live bypass today, but revocation of this write depends entirely on the name-list and on ruler teardown ordering rather than on the handle, which is the property the rest of the change was built to stop relying on.

samples.summary: `pageSetupGuardedStore` now binds its members to the revocable Proxy, so its own doc comment ("no implementation ever observes the proxy as `this`") no longer describes what the code guarantees
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3315` changes the proxy target from `docStore` to `revocableStore`, and `:3322` does `raw.bind(target)` with `target` now being that Proxy. The stated invariant at `:3290-3293` ("Members resolve off the real store and are bound to it") holds only incidentally: `revocableDocStore`'s `get` already returns a function bound to the real store (`packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:202`), and re-binding a bound function cannot change its `this`. For a `readOnly` mount `revocableStore === docStore`, so the two mounts reach the same result by different routes. No behavioural break found (member identity is still stable through the double memoization, and a `vi.spyOn` on the underlying store still invalidates both caches), but the comment should be corrected before the next edit to either wrapper.
